relevance_note: Case report of an adult with GAMT deficiency plus per-patient literature tables of 28 further adults and 124 children: "Whole‐exome sequencing identified novel compound heterozygous GAMT variants (c.265_267del and c.253G>T)".
method_note: Built with a Python script (scratch build.py) that transcribes Tables 1-3, Table S1 and Table S2 row by row; every span is a contiguous row prefix from the patient number through the cell used, and all spans were checked verbatim by script. Scope: the index case (first-hand), 28 previously published adults (Table 1/2/3/S2, No. 2-29) and 124 previously published children (Table S1, Case No. 1-124); each table row is one person and nobody was merged. Labels: adults the text names as 'Patient N' (2, 4, 5, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 19, 25, 26, 27, 29) are 'Patient N'; other adults use the No. column ('Table 1 #N'), including the index case ('Table 1 #1', called only 'our case'/'the proband'); children are 'Table S1 #N'. Table 1 'Age reported (exam or diagnosed)' and Table S1 'Age diagnosed or reported' are ambiguous between age at diagnosis and at report; recorded as age at last evaluation, ISO only when one number is given. V/X symbols are defined in the legends ('V, positive history; X, negative history'; 'V = positive history; X = negative history'), quoted as second spans. Variant pairing: within one person's row, the Table S1 cDNA/protein cells (' / ' separated) and Table 1 genotype/mutation-type cells ('; ' and '/' separated) were paired by position across that person's own two alleles (not across people); Table S1 'Mutation type (1)/(2)' columns were mapped to the first/second variant. Zygosity left not reported for all literature patients (the paper gives only cohort counts: 22 homozygotes, 4 compound heterozygotes, without naming them). Adult variants for No. 17, 26, 27 are NR in Table 1 (no variant rows). No. 14 (Patient 14) never had molecular testing; Table 1 lists c.59G > C^b, which the text says was presumed from her twin; the row is kept but is presumed, not tested. Protein p.Trp20Ser added to adult c.59G > C rows from the sentence naming that exact variant. ALPL and POLG VUS in the index case are named but not described and get no rows. Checklist: broad absences ('No involuntary movements', 'No extrapyramidal movement disorder', Table S1 Movement disorder = X, PIND = X, 'No Autism') were recorded as excluded phenotypic_features rows only and not used to exclude narrower checklist items. Table S1 Movement disorder maps to no checklist item. Paraparesis, rigidity, hypertonia and attention deficit were not mapped to checklist items. Hand clasping (No. 28) was not counted as a stereotypy. Patient 29 'Social interaction deficit' was mapped to autistic features. Contradictions/notes: (1) Table 3 row 1 gives ornithine X and arginine restriction X for the index case, but the text says arginine restriction and ornithine supplementation (100 mg/kg/day) were initiated; the text was used for treatment_summary. (2) The text says epilepsy was documented in 27 of 29 adults with only Patients 19 (no seizures) and 27 (no data) excepted, but Tables 2/3 give Patient 14 NA; seizures left not reported for Patient 14. (3) Table S1 counts (ID/DD V=122, Epilepsy V=93, Movement disorder V=42 of 124) differ by one each from the text/Table S4 pediatric totals (121, 92 and 41). (4) Table S1 #21 lists c.327G>A with type Missense although c.327G>A is called Splicing elsewhere; recorded as stated. (5) Table 2 has empty seizure-type/EEG cells for rows 1, 4, 5, 28, 29 (probably multi-line cells lost in conversion). (6) Table S1 #116 second allele is printed only as '(?)' with type 'Transcription (null)'; kept as a variant row with variant string 'not reported'. n_patients_reported = 150 from 'In this largest (n = 150) analytical cohort' (26 adults with molecular details + 124 children); the 29+124 = 153 total is never stated as one number, so cohort_size_as_stated is null. Study type recorded as 'case report' though most individuals come from the literature review.
